overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email on September 4 when a councilor copied the entire Council on her opinions; the August 1 email and Facebook remarks were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council deliberated outside a posted meeting by email when a councilor copied the whole Council on a September 4 reply defending a salary vote.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Council deliberated outside of a properly noticed meeting via email on September 4 in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a councilor's August 1 email copied to the whole Council was deliberation; the complaint was filed more than thirty days later.
allegations.key_passage: Because the September 5 complaint, as it relates to the August 1 email, was not timely filed with the Council, we decline to review the allegation relating to the August 1 email.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a councilor retaliated for an open meeting complaint through offensive and harassing Facebook comments.
allegations.key_passage: An allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility towards a member of the public does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Release the September 4 email to the public within 30 days of receipt of the determination.
